newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open 0.53 pct lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open 0.53 pct lower on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares opened lower on profit-taking after fresh highs last week and with investors pondering the outlook for French shares which seem to have become expensive, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 12.34 points or 0.55 percent at 2,227.99 at 0905 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 16 points at 2,233.
On Friday the CAC-40 had hit a year high of 2,2250.29, getting back to levels seen in early 1994 when the index reached its all time high at 2,360.98 points.

A recent poll of 16 brokers showed the average forecast for the CAC-40 is at 2,176.43 in three months and 2,313.33 in a year. According to brokers CCF Elysees Bourse, French shares are trading at an average price/earnings ratio of 16.2 on 1997 earnings, assuming 25 percent profit growth in 1997.

Via Banque jumped 4.6 percent at the opening to 166.10 on expectations Banque Paribas will sell the unit, part of the Navigation Mixte holding company of which it took possesion earlier this year and is now busy selling assets. On Friday, Paribas said the bank was not for sale "today" but had no place in Paribas over the long term.
Paribas itself fell 1.8 percent to 362 francs at 0917 GMT, after a 12 percent rally last week.
Car maker Renault, which rose on Friday despite weak sales figures and a profit warning, joined the downward trend on Monday and dropped 2.19 percent to 120.40 francs.

Euro Disney started unchanged at 10.65 francs. The leisure parc operator will announce its 1995/96 results on Tuesday, expected to post its second annual profit with analysts forecasting a figure of between 160 and 200 million.
Sligos and Axime, set for merger, down over five percent after gains last week when suspensions ended.
